path: PING_TRANSACTION -> IPCObjectStub::SendRequest -> DBinderPingTransaction -> reply int32 / transport return

overlap.challenge: Fixed ERR_NONE reply holds only if reply.WriteInt32 succeeds. Intended observable effect is a transport liveness result; no OnRemoteRequest callback is dispatched. But ‘no effect’ is too broad: an authorized holder may learn whether a handle responds. That is intended framework ping behavior absent evidence of a sensitive unauthorized target.
overlap.feedback_sent: Asked D70 to distinguish helper, dispatcher and driver; characterize liveness disclosure; compare unknown code and recording stub controls.

source_conclusions.entry: IPCObjectStub::SendRequest switches PING_TRANSACTION directly to DBinderPingTransaction. Handler ignores code/data/option and caller identity, writes ERR_NONE; write failure returns IPC_STUB_WRITE_PARCEL_ERR, otherwise ERR_NONE.
source_conclusions.framework_caller: BinderInvoker::PingService sends empty parcel and PING_TRANSACTION for handle; IPCProcessSkeleton calls it for REGISTRY_HANDLE while acquiring a new registry proxy.
source_conclusions.proxy_control: PING_TRANSACTION is packed '_PNG' (0x5f504e47), above MAX_TRANSACTION_ID 0x00ffffff; ordinary IPCObjectProxy::SendRequest rejects it before transport. This does not prove raw Binder driver transactions impossible.
source_conclusions.unknowns: Raw driver caller/handle policy, cross-process handle transfer, target sensitivity, UID/PID/token checks, kernel behavior and product transport are not closed.

oracle.preconditions: Matching IPC source/build and product config, actual Binder driver, two controlled processes, recorded stub and documented handle transfer/permission rules.
oracle.positive: Live valid registry object: transaction returns ERR_NONE, reply is exactly one int32 ERR_NONE, recording OnRemoteRequest count/state unchanged.
negative_controls: Unknown code below MAX_TRANSACTION_ID dispatches to recording OnRemoteRequest and increments count; PING does not.
Public proxy PING returns IPC_PROXY_INVALID_CODE_ERR without transport.
No-handle and stale-handle attempts fail without callback, compared with same caller holding a valid handle.
Privileged intended holder versus low-privilege valid-handle holder: any differing access is only a liveness disclosure until sensitive target/policy violation is demonstrated.
Mock WriteInt32 failure returns IPC_STUB_WRITE_PARCEL_ERR; this is not remotely attacker-controlled evidence.
oracle.falsifier: Proxy rejects the code; driver denies callers without a handle; holders are authorized to observe liveness; no sensitive unauthorized effect exists.
oracle.not_proven: No product test or liveness-confidentiality impact was executed or established.

candidate_assessment.result: No candidate. Source-bound mechanism is intended liveness probe; unauthorized caller, sensitive target, or violated policy/security effect not proven.
candidate_assessment.possible_followup: If a product owner identifies a sensitive service whose valid handle is available to a lower-privilege principal contrary to policy, run the oracle and then reassess; do not create a detector rule on current evidence.
